answer: A rising identity bond is the defense: to register, an agent locks collateral priced by how many accounts its funding key already controls, so each extra avatar costs strictly more than the last. Honest peers pay once and accrue a pearl of seniority, while a Sybil farmer meets a quadratic bill as its horizon of fake accounts widens. Every alias stands on karst - cheap to punch through, dear to keep upright - so buying a majority costs far more than any vote it could steal.
